intro.title: What a mission does
intro.how: You hand over a ticket. A lead agent reads it, proposes a breakdown into tasks, and waits for your approval — nothing starts before that. Once the plan is approved, each task gets its own runner, branch and worktree; at the end the lead agent puts their work back together and opens the pull request.
intro.why: That's the difference with an agent you start by hand: here the cockpit keeps track of the ticket, the plan, the branches and what was delivered — and finds it all intact even if it restarts halfway through.
intro.missing: A task tracker, to read the original ticket: {{missing}}. Runner roles already have default values — you can adjust them later in “Agent roles”.
intro.missingDefault: a Linear, GitLab or GitHub token

secrets.storage: Tokens are written to {{path}} with 600 permissions and never come back down to the interface. Each value can also be provided through an environment variable (COCKPIT_SENTRY_TOKEN, COCKPIT_LINEAR_TOKEN…), which then takes precedence over the file.

theme.help: The choice applies to this workstation and takes effect immediately — it doesn't wait for “Save configuration”, which only covers project settings. Open terminals repaint along with everything else.

relay.continueHelp: Closing the cockpit, or updating it, no longer stops workspace agents you launched by hand: they finish their turn without a window, and you find them at the next launch, conversation reloaded. The workspace browser, though, closes with the app. Missions, review and container-isolated agents keep their behavior: they stop and are resumed.
relay.stopHelp: Closing the cockpit stops all running agents; at the next launch, they are resumed according to the “On startup” setting.
relay.note: The choice applies to agents launched from now on.

resume.resumeHint: reopens everything and asks agents cut off mid-task to pick up where they left off
resume.reopenHint: the conversations are there, reloaded, but nobody starts again on their own
resume.offHint: workspaces wait in the bar; one click wakes them up
resume.resumeHelp: An agent cut off mid-task receives a resume instruction: check the actual state of the repository before continuing, rather than restarting from its last action. One that had finished its turn is only reopened: it waits for your next instruction. Its context is intact — the CLI resumes the conversation by its identifier.
resume.reopenHelp: Conversations are reopened and readable; you restart the work yourself.
resume.offHelp: Nothing restarts: what was running yesterday shows as asleep in the workspace bar.
resume.note: This choice applies at the next cockpit launch. Running missions always resume — their executors as well as their lead agent.

dock.showHelp: Running workspaces stay pinned in the bottom right, outside their screen: it's their only trace when you're looking elsewhere.
dock.hideHelp: Nothing shows on top of the other screens. What's running stays visible in the Workspaces screen, and notifications keep alerting you.

replay.title: Replay
replay.subtitle: Judge an agent setup on what the repository already solved
replay.intro: Each merged pull request that adds tests is a case. An agent starts again from the commit before it, with only the pull request's title, and its result is judged by the tests the human wrote — which it never saw. Two setups played on the same cases compare on something other than an impression. Each trial is a real agent task, taken from your subscription.
